instrument_name: AS 23.15.630 Special employee unemployment credit and contributions for program (STEP)
figure_or_rule_carried: Department collects from each employee one-tenth of one percent (0.10%) of wages (AS 23.20.175) on which the employee contributes under AS 23.20.290(d); employee credited the same amount against unemployment contributions owed, so net nil; programme AS 23.15.620 State training and employment program

instrument_name: Alaska ES Tax Forms and Publications index (complete list of programme forms)
figure_or_rule_carried: Index lists Handbook, registration, quarterly contribution report, supplemental/correction, online filing specs, refund, option forms, tax clearance, Power of Attorney; no form or publication for disability insurance, paid family/medical leave or any levy other than UI (STEP/TVEP are inside the UI report). Absence on the full programme index; no express negative statement

instrument_name: Alaska SB 217 employer STEP tax 0.4 percent, effective 2027-01-01 (lead from search summary only)
figure_or_rule_carried: Search summary says employers contribute 0.4 percent of wages under AS 23.20.290(c) as STEP tax with credit for UI contributions paid; effective 2027-01-01. NOT read from primary text; outside 2026 scope; verify before use

instrument_name: 32 V.S.A. 5825 Credit for taxes paid to other states and provinces
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident taxpayer credit against 5822 tax for income tax paid to another state, DC or Canadian province on income from sources there, capped at the Vermont tax attributable to that income; 5825(b) deemed-resident domiciliaries get credit only if domicile jurisdiction gives a similar credit

instrument_name: Vermont Income Tax Withholding for Employees (individuals page)
figure_or_rule_carried: Page states payments to a nonresident for services performed in Vermont are subject to withholding; no reciprocity or reciprocal agreement mention (absence on this page)

instrument_name: Vermont Withholding page: out-of-state employers 30-day rule
figure_or_rule_carried: Out-of-state employers need not begin Vermont withholding until an employee has worked from a Vermont location for thirty days; no reciprocity agreement mention. With GB-1210-2026 (US-VT-P5-1-003), FAQ (US-VT-P5-1-014), individuals page (US-VT-P5-2-002) and 32 V.S.A. 5841 (US-VT-P5-1-001): four official withholding texts, none lists a reciprocity agreement; conclusion: no reciprocity agreement published

instrument_name: Vermont DOL WH-13 re-read: wage statement duty and its cited authority
authority: Vermont Department of Labor Wage and Hour Program
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers must provide a wage statement with each payment of wages: total hours worked, hourly rate, gross pay, each deduction fully itemized. The only statutory cite on that page, 21 V.S.A. 342(d), is attached to the direct-deposit sentence, not to the statement; a search summary that attributed the statement to 342(d) is not supported

instrument_name: Vermont Act 40 of 2025 (S.117) wage and hour amendments scan
figure_or_rule_carried: Full-text scan of 19 pages: no wage-statement or itemised-deduction text (amends 342a investigation of unpaid wages and unemployment/workers compensation provisions); the statement duty is not added by statute in this act

instrument_name: Wyoming DWS Unemployment Tax Rates page (full read in Chrome)
figure_or_rule_carried: Rates assigned per W.S. 27-3 Art. 5. New employers (under three years experience) get a base rate by their industry plus four additional rate factors; rate notice issued on completing Joint Business Registration; if registration is not completed before the first report the highest base rate applies, 8.5 percent. No numeric 2026 industry table on the page (rate notice and helpline 307-235-3217 only): the numeric new-employer rate is not published on the programme page
